rule: Only Albert's own yes completes an item. Days are his estimates; the plan is one work-day per calendar day, the categories in his order.

categories.name: Primary art
categories.desc: The characters and their animation: the four rats from the side and from above, the mole, the cat statues and what they wear. You estimated about 90% done with one day of work left.

categories.name: Secondary art
categories.desc: Everything else you see: every minigame's backgrounds, props, pickups and effects, the lobby and the piñata screen, the flowers and small pieces, and the UI and HUD art. A piece an agent made counts only once you've checked and approved it in a live session.

categories.name: Mechanics
categories.desc: The core gameplay of the minigames and the party around them. You estimated it 99% done; what is left here are the adjustments and the known bugs.

categories.name: Music
categories.desc: About thirty tracks: the menus, the lobby, the screens between games and one for each minigame, each picked by your ear.

categories.name: Sound effects
categories.desc: Every sound the game makes, family by family: buttons, countdowns, the rats, the lobby, the score screen, the piñata and each minigame.

categories.name: Game feel
categories.desc: The final polish on how everything feels: shake, hit pauses, flashes, haptics, transitions and the big payoff moments.

categories.name: Playtesting
categories.desc: The game on real phones with real players, and the fixes that turns up.

categories.name: Marketing
categories.desc: Everything that has to exist before the game can earn: the icon and key art, store pages, screenshots and trailer, socials, the dev vlog and the launch itself.
